title: Route agentgov next through the guided development lifecycle

requirement.summary: Continue ADR-0009 productization by making the existing read-only agentgov next command select exactly one safe development action after onboarding and deterministic repository failures are handled.

objective.rationale: Users should not need to reconstruct the start, check, finish, and Monitor sequence from low-level state, while every write and authority boundary remains owned by the existing commands.

goal: Extend agentgov next with deterministic, read-only routing for no session, active start, scope result, incomplete completion evidence, verified completion, and invalid local-state conditions.
non_goals: Do not execute the selected command, create or replace a task, write local state, run validation, generate a Monitor, or modify Git state.
Do not weaken onboarding conflict, missing-scaffold, or deterministic repository FAIL precedence.
Do not infer semantic task choice among multiple admitted tasks or claim that a recommended command is approved.
Do not add hooks, a daemon, background monitoring, exception records, action-loop self-reporting, a 0.3 release, consumer migration, merge, or deployment.
Preserve the existing uncommitted opt-in Monitor artifact slice without changing its implementation or authority boundary.
acceptance_signals: Adoption conflicts, missing scaffold, and deterministic repository FAIL remain ahead of development routing.
With no active session, next recommends a dry-run govern start without choosing semantically among multiple tasks.
A valid active session routes task.started to govern check, a passed scope check to govern finish, incomplete or stale completion to govern finish, and verified completion to monitor development.
Malformed, tracked, missing-start, task-drifted, or conflicting local state fails closed as one blocking action and no file is changed.
Repository WARN and ADVISORY findings remain available through repository checks but no longer displace the active guided development lifecycle.
Text and strict JSON still contain exactly one action and preserve action_executed=false, modifies_repository=false, and denied Git/release authority.
The existing next-action schema remains structurally compatible and all focused and repository tests pass.

items: A wrong precedence could hide a deterministic repository failure or send a user into an invalid active session.
Old events from a prior session could be mistaken for current progress if session identity and start time are not enforced.
A recommendation could be mistaken for execution or human approval.

stop_conditions: Stop if selecting an action requires writing, deleting, repairing, or normalizing local state.
Stop if the route must guess which of multiple admitted tasks matches human intent.
Stop if invalid task, session, event, or comparison-base identity cannot be surfaced as a blocking result.
Stop if the change requires weakening existing stable onboarding or repository-failure behavior.

decision.rationale: The user explicitly authorized the recommended next productization slice and retained separate control of commit, push, release, and deployment. The delivered task was paused on 2026-08-05 to remove it from automatic discovery; this is routing hygiene, not a claim of semantic completion, acceptance, merge, or release.
